bug_semantics: Integer overflow to heap overflow in ggml-org/llama.cpp llama_batch_init(): attacker-influenced n_tokens_alloc, embd, and n_seq_max are multiplied into malloc() sizes with no range/overflow checks, so the products wrap (INT32_MAX / size_t) and undersize the token/embd/pos/seq_id/logits buffers. Later batch fills write past those allocations, causing heap corruption and potential code execution. CWE-190/CWE-680. CVE.org PUBLISHED; not withdrawn.
flaw_origin: Georgi Gerganov first wrote llama_batch_init() in reconstructable PR #3228 member addae65fd44d362995acd8c05b99c3351c214df8 (2023-09-20, llama.cpp/llama.h) with unchecked malloc(sizeof(float)*n_tokens*embd) and sibling size multiplies. That member is absent from its parent a1327c71c6cfee3b1697aa6646f52f1de249120b. GitHub squash-merged the PR as ec893798b7a2a803466cc8f063051499ec3d96f7, tagged b1283 (advisory start). #3624 0e89203b517c95ec6675eda75d200a60d1e8921d later added the n_seq_max per-token seq_id malloc, widening the same sink. No overflow checks on b9058, b9445, or master HEAD.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-43627 is a real CWE-190 integer overflow in llama_batch_init() malloc size math. The first-party NVD/GHSA/VulnCheck text matches the still-live function: n_tokens_alloc*embd and sizeof(llama_seq_id)*n_seq_max can wrap, then batch operations write past the undersized heap. CVE.org is PUBLISHED, not withdrawn, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. BIC search started from that sink, not from AI markers. git log of PR #3228 members plus parent-tree grep shows the helper first appears in addae65fd44d362995acd8c05b99c3351c214df8; earlier PR members and parent a1327c71c6cfee3b1697aa6646f52f1de249120b lack llama_batch_init entirely. The master squash ec893798b7a2a803466cc8f063051499ec3d96f7 is a squash aggregate (tag b1283), so it is not the BIC; the reconstructable member is. #3624 later added the n_seq_max multiply Cyera highlights, which widens the same unchecked-malloc mechanism rather than first writing it; CVE affected range correctly starts at b1283. AI judgment is BIC-only: addae65 is human-authored by Georgi Gerganov with no commit-object AI trailers or bot identity, so NOT_AI. Closed PR #24063 and the Cyera patches repo are remediations, not introducers. No upstream fix landed through master c841aeeb8bb2fe417038dadfa9b007cf1a9ef950; the finding is unpatched.
remaining_gap: Upstream ggml-org/llama.cpp remains unpatched (no merged fix SHA). Closed PR #24063 was not landed; Cyera third-party patch is mitigation only.

unpatched.reason: Vendor closed GHSA-wwq5-4jr6-6m93 without a fix (2026-01-05) and closed public PR ggml-org/llama.cpp#24063 without merging. llama_batch_init() at b9058, Cyera's b9445 re-check, and master HEAD c841aeeb8bb2fe417038dadfa9b007cf1a9ef950 still multiply n_tokens_alloc/embd/n_seq_max into malloc() with no overflow checks. CVE lists no patched version (defaultStatus=affected).

potential_fix.approach: In llama_batch_init(), reject n_tokens_alloc<=0, n_seq_max<=0, embd<0, and n_tokens_alloc>=INT32_MAX; refuse malloc size products that exceed SIZE_MAX/sizeof(float)/embd or SIZE_MAX/sizeof(llama_seq_id) before calling malloc; return a zeroed batch on failure.
potential_fix.rationale: Those checks stop wrapping allocation sizes so later token/embd/seq_id/logits writes cannot run past the heap buffers. Matches Cyera's CVE-2026-43627-batch-init-overflow.patch.
